champion: Sister Mary Joseph nodule due to transverse colon cancer
ordered_diagnoses: Sister Mary Joseph nodule due to transverse colon cancer

facts.raw_span: A 55-year-old man
no significant medical history
10-month history of spontaneous, progressively painful umbilical discomfort
a firm nodule at the umbilicus that gradually increased in size and became ulcerated and tender
The umbilical lesion measured 6 cm by 6 cm, was ulcerated over its entire surface, and bled on contact
Deep palpation of the abdomen revealed a poorly defined, firm mass approximately 8 cm in diameter in the right hypochondrium
Biopsy of the umbilical lesion demonstrated a well-differentiated, infiltrating adenocarcinoma

Contrast-enhanced abdominal CT showed homogeneously enhancing umbilical tissue growth and irregular, circumferential thickening of the right third of the transverse colon measuring approximately 8.3 cm
Total colonoscopy revealed no endoluminal lesion

concepts.preferred_label: Sister Mary Joseph nodule due to transverse colon cancer
concepts.why: The presence of a painful umbilical nodule with ulceration, a firm mass in the right hypochondrium, and biopsy-proven adenocarcinoma, along with CT findings of umbilical tissue growth and colon thickening, suggests metastasis to the umbilicus from a primary colon cancer.

The combination of a firm mass in the right hypochondrium, biopsy-proven adenocarcinoma, and CT findings of irregular colon thickening supports the diagnosis of primary colon cancer in the transverse colon.
It explains the umbilical nodule in the context of abdominal cancer.

rationales.F08: Imaging findings of umbilical tissue growth and colon thickening are highly consistent with Sister Mary Joseph nodule due to transverse colon cancer
